citation.title: Hey Robot, the Mind Is Not Enough to Join the Moral Community! The Effect of Assigning a Mind and a Soul to a Humanoid Robot on Its Moral Status

reading.source_scope_note: One cross-sectional Polish-language online survey about a static description/photo of Sophia. Prose reports390 respondents,167 excluded and223 believers in both mind and soul retained; Table1 counts total394. Measures are human attributions and moral-status ratings, not actual robot consciousness, soul, moral agency or established rights. Same-sample PCA and path analysis do not identify causal mediation, metaphysical truth or a universal criterion for moral standing.
access_limits: All19 supplied pages read. DOI web-reader failed, but the ordinary public publisher page and PDF were accessible. Downloadhttps://czasopisma.tnkul.pl/index.php/rpsych/article/download/564/382/1109 checksum-matched. The supplement is embedded in the read PDF; no additional original studies were read by following its citations.

No accessible raw data, model syntax, registration, exact final sample per analysis, missingness flow or effect-size calculation file was identified on the inspected publisher page. No author contact, respondent profiling, author-code execution or independent new survey.

Participants include ages15–70. The supplied paper does not state an explicit ethics/parental-consent procedure; this is a documentation limit, not proof of absent consent or wrongdoing. Individual religious affiliation, conservatism and anthropocentrism were not listed as measured demographics; do not infer them from language, nationality or the authors’ contextual description.

Primary Crossref verifies Johnson/Verdicchio2018 pagination and Richert/Harris2008 identity only. Those originals, Gray2007, Warren1997, religious traditions, cited books and the in-preparation intercultural study were not fully read in this step. No invented missing source or extra full-reading credit.
No real human–robot interaction, behavior toward a robot, factual test of a soul, new language-model experiment, whole-paper Markdown archive, extra page or principle.

study.sample: Prose:390 Polish-speaking respondents, age15–70,M32.29,SD13.59;167 excluded because they did not affirm both mind and soul;223 retained,M34.00,SD13.91,62.3%female. This arithmetic reconciles. Table1 instead has394 mind responses and394 soul responses. The table/prose sample flow is unresolved; do not replace the reported primaryN with a guessed correction.
study.selection: Analysis is deliberately restricted to people affirming both concepts. It does not describe all Polish people, all believers, every religion or nonbelievers. Conditioning on such beliefs can affect associations and generalization. Authors explicitly acknowledge cultural/language scope, sample selection, size and correlational design.
study.procedure: Google Forms, static description and photo of Sophia at the2018AIforGOODsummit. Moral status is rated first, then attributes and robot mind/soul, then human ontological beliefs and demographics. No randomized attribution manipulation or temporal mediator sequence. Reverse attribution from initial moral concern, shared beliefs and response consistency remain possible.
study.soul_and_mind: Separate single five-point statements Sophia has a mind and Sophia has a soul. Reported means2.20 and1.20 are both below scale midpoint3; more mind than soul is a relative attribution result, not majority endorsement of a robot mind. Soul attribution is the narrower component of the existing Animism definition, which explicitly includes attribution of a soul; preserve the term in research notes without an alias asserting exact equivalence.
study.components: Methods list five attributes while saying six; supplementaryS1 supplies memory as the sixth. PCA/varimax yields Experience(emotion,pain,consciousness) and Agency(planning,memory,self-control), alphas.84/.67. Bartlettdf15 fits six variables. Eigenvalues2.33/1.87 and38.84%+31.19%=70.03% broadly reconcile. This is same-sample component extraction, not independent confirmation of universally two mental dimensions.
study.moral_status: Seven heterogeneous items mix destruction, pain, life/freedom, human rights, environmental significance, social obligations and citizenship. Alpha rises.52to.78 after dropping the destruction item. Reverse-coding and a multidimensional validity analysis are not supplied; do not assert that scoring definitely omitted reversal. Predictor pain and outcome pain content overlap. One scale does not settle moral agency, standing and legal personhood.
study.paths: Figure1 shows mind→Experience.591, mind→Agency.328, mind→Status.036, soul→Status.122, Experience→Status.593, Agency→Status.200, mind–soul covariance/correlation.410. Standardized indirect products.350463/.0656 broadly match.351/.065 after rounding. A nonzero conditional association does not demonstrate causal mediation or a necessary/sufficient soul condition.
study.intervals: Table3 explicitly gives unstandardized indirect estimates.219/.041 with90%CIs[.169,.276]/[.024,.063], alongside standardized values.351/.065. Those intervals contain their unstandardized estimates; comparing them directly with standardized beta would be a false criticism. Other paths’ interval scales need explicit labeling; do not invent corrected intervals or convert90%to95%.
study.fit: ReportedCMIN/DF.53,CFI1,SRMR.034,RMSEA0with90%upper.111 can occur for a small-df model. Point fit does not prove causal direction, unique model or excellent population fit; the wide upper bound matters. Original covariance/model output is unavailable.
study.sample_ambiguity: Table2 means2.29/1.22 differ from text2.20/1.20, and mind–soulr.41 versus text.42. Soul–Agencyr.15 is markedp<.01, whereas an ordinary two-sided correlation test givesp≈.025 forN223 but≈.0028 forN394. This is compatible with a different analysis sample but does not prove which sample was used. Ask for per-analysisN instead of relabeling everyone asN394.
study.effect_sizes: For pairedt222, standardized changedz=t/sqrt223 gives≈.744 for mind versus soul. Supplementary six values are≈.447,.228,.623,.758,.868,.702. Published d labels1.33 and1.98/2.12/1.86/1.84/1.89/1.76 are not those values and closely track raw SDs of paired differences. The intended formula is unavailable; retain this reproducibility concern without pretending dz is the only possible convention.
study.belief_tables: S2/S3 distributions reconcile to100% after rounding. S4 mind52%ceases, so48%does not; soul6.7%ceases, so93.3%does not. The latter includes2.2%nothingchanges,78.5%afterlife,12.6%reincarnation. Later78.5%is afterlife alone, not the entire complement. Distinguish category groupings rather than falsely call every93.3versus78.5difference arithmetic error.
study.inference: Culturally situated ratings are data about beliefs, not demonstrations that Sophia is conscious or has a soul. Conceptual mind/soul distinction can coexist with their observed correlation; correlation.42 does not establish statistical independence. Moral standing does not logically entail agency, responsibility or legal personhood, and human dignity must not depend on a survey’s religious criterion.

summary: No new row. Preserve Soul perception/Soul attribution as a narrower component in the existing Animism record; enrich existing mind, agency, experience and moral-standing attributions. Document genuine sample/percentage and effect-size questions while retaining coherent PCA arithmetic, path products and unstandardized confidence intervals. Perceived status and metaphysical claims remain separate.

findings.definition: Attributing life, vitality or a soul to nonhuman entities, including objects or features of nature.
findings.novelty_rationale: Use the existing concept and preserve the narrower measure or scope. A new label, survey item or robot example does not justify a duplicate row.
findings.evidence_scope: Soul attribution (called Soul perception in the paper) is measured by a single five-point statement and related to attributed moral status. It is conceptually distinguished from attributing cognitive capacities, although mind/soul scores are correlated. The existing Animism definition already includes attributing a soul to a nonhuman entity.
findings.boundary: This is a narrower component, not an exact synonym of all animism or a new independent behavior. A reported attribution does not verify a soul, imply irrationality or identify a person’s religion. Single-item, selected-sample correlations do not establish a causal, necessary or sufficient condition for moral standing.

findings.definition: Ascribing or denying mental capacities to another entity.
findings.novelty_rationale: Use the existing concept and preserve the narrower measure or scope. A new label, survey item or robot example does not justify a duplicate row.
findings.evidence_scope: The survey distinguishes a global mind-attribution item from attributed mental capacities and the soul item. PCA on six capacity ratings produces two components in this sample.
findings.boundary: Attributions do not verify possession. One-robot participant-level covariance differs from earlier analyses aggregating many entities. A two-component solution here neither refutes every one-dimensional account nor proves a universal two-dimensional mental mechanism. Global mind ratings below midpoint are not majority acceptance.

findings.definition: Attributing to another entity the capacity for subjective feelings or sensations, such as pleasure, pain, fear or joy.
findings.novelty_rationale: Use the existing concept and preserve the narrower measure or scope. A new label, survey item or robot example does not justify a duplicate row.
findings.evidence_scope: A component of three robot-capacity ratings, labeled Experience, is positively associated with attributed moral status in the reported path model.
findings.boundary: This measures human ascriptions, not actual subjective experience. Pain content appears in predictor and status items, creating potential content overlap. Same-sample associations and90%bootstrap intervals do not identify a causal effect or normative rights criterion.

findings.definition: Attributing to another entity a capacity for intentional thought, planning and action.
findings.novelty_rationale: Use the existing concept and preserve the narrower measure or scope. A new label, survey item or robot example does not justify a duplicate row.
findings.evidence_scope: Planning, memory and self-control ratings form the component labeled Agency, with reported alpha.67 and a positive conditional status association.
findings.boundary: Cognitive agency ratings are not demonstrated moral competence, actual capacity or legal accountability. A moderate alpha and same-sample PCA do not validate a universal agency factor; memory/planning do not by themselves entail moral responsibility.

findings.definition: Attributing to an entity a claim to moral consideration in how actions affect it.

evidence.quote: Should Sophia be granted human rights?

findings.novelty_rationale: Use the existing concept and preserve the narrower measure or scope. A new label, survey item or robot example does not justify a duplicate row.
findings.evidence_scope: A six-item post-deletion composite combines attributed protections, rights, susceptibility to harm and relational obligations. It correlates with mind, experience, agency and soul attributions in this selected sample.
findings.boundary: An attributed status is not a justified universal rule or actual legal right. Moral patients need not be moral agents, and legal personhood is a further distinction. The paper’s broad suggestion that entities without souls lack rights does not follow from these ratings and cannot be extended to human dignity.

findings.definition: Attributing to an entity the capacity to understand moral considerations, make ethical judgments and bear responsibility for its choices.

evidence.quote: artificial individuals become autonomous moral agents

findings.novelty_rationale: Use the existing concept and preserve the narrower measure or scope. A new label, survey item or robot example does not justify a duplicate row.
findings.evidence_scope: The theoretical discussion moves from granting moral status to agenthood and responsibility.
findings.boundary: Context only: the study measures perceived cognitive capacities and attributed status, not autonomous ethical action or justified responsibility. Keep standing, moral agency and legal personhood separate rather than import that inference into the ontology.

aggregate_checks.scope: Aggregate arithmetic only. Keep N390 in prose and394 in Table1 as an unresolved source discrepancy; do not substitute a corrected analysis sample.

s1.label: Mind versus soul assigned to Sophia

aggregate_checks.effect_size_boundary: Reported d values resemble the unstandardized standard deviation of paired differences. The paired standardized change dz=t/sqrt(N) is shown as an explicit alternative convention, not a claim to recover the authors’ intended formula. Original data/calculation are required.

after_death.boundary: Different response groupings answer different questions.93.3 includes nothing-changes2.2,afterlife78.5,reincarnation12.6. Do not silently label it afterlife-only.

source_corrections.correction: Counts95and73 correspond to24.1%and18.5%of394, whereas printed Not sure and No percentages are18.5%and24.1%. The two percentage labels are exchanged if those counts and that denominator are correct. Preserve the separate unresolved394versus390sample issue; do not silently change counts or recruitment totals.

SupplementS1 includes six attributes, adding Memory to the five named in the methods list. Bartlettdf15 and factor descriptions are consistent with six variables. Correct the descriptive list rather than allege an impossible five-variable/six-variable analysis.
Why robots should not be treated like animals is Ethics and Information Technology20(4):291–301, not the truncated291–30. Metadata only; the original was not fully read.

Attributing moral consideration does not logically entail moral agency, responsibility or legal personhood. Correlational soul/status ratings do not establish that a soul is necessary or sufficient for full moral status. Preserve this as a boundary of the paper’s inference, not an empirical verdict on religion or machine metaphysics.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: Prose390−167=223 reconciles, but each Table1 count column sums394. Table2 means and correlation-star behavior may reflect a different sample. Original participant flow and per-analysisN are required; no recovered corrected recruitment or path-analysisN.

Reported values closely resemble SDs of paired differences rather than conventional standardized changes derived from the pairedt values. Explicit dz alternatives and successful p checks are retained. Need intended estimator and original calculations; no claim to have rerun raw data or recovered the authors’ formula.

Table3 clarifies unstandardized indirect intervals, but prose mixes standardized beta and intervals for other paths without equally explicit scale labels. Request output/labels rather than declare intervals wrong because they exclude standardized beta.

No independent validation sample, original reverse-scoring details, full model alternatives or raw covariance is supplied. Deleting the destruction item may reflect wording/scoring or heterogeneity; lack of documentation does not prove a particular mistake.

The scale/theory cites Warr/Warren1997 without a matching bibliography entry; Richert/Harris2006 is cited but only2008appears in the bibliography, and Gladden2014in text conflicts with2016entry. Complete intended identities are needed. Do not invent a missing DOI or count an in-preparation intercultural manuscript as published primary evidence.

Selected Polish-language respondents are not a probability sample of Western culture. Individual religiosity/conservatism was not listed as measured; the author’s contextual description is not a diagnosis of every participant. Age range includes minors and explicit consent/ethics details are absent in this supplied text; documentation uncertainty is not proof of misconduct.

refuted_suspected_errors.finding: A small-df model can yieldCFI1andRMSEA0, while its upper interval.111 remains wide. Neither fabrication nor causal truth follows from those point indices.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: Soul perception requires a separate row despite explicit existing coverage
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: The retained Animism definition already covers assigning a soul to nonhuman entities. Keep a narrower research note, not a second broad row or an alias equating all animism with soul attribution.
They explicitly call the design correlational, acknowledge belief-based selection/cultural scope and propose larger and experimental studies.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Animism already includes soul attribution. Preserve the narrower measured component and do not infer a uniform religious worldview, a causal nationality effect or actual machine experience.
Mind-perception dimensionality depends on capacities, entities and aggregation level. Distinguish one-robot respondent covariance from multi-entity aggregate structure.
Compare coefficients and intervals only on the same scale/model. Separate successful arithmetic checks from genuine source discrepancies.

deferred.reason: Narrower aspect of the existing Animism definition. Preserve the name in its research note without an exact-synonym alias or duplicate row.

deferred.reason: Secondary theoretical discussion is not a new observed expansion process or a necessary/sufficient criterion. Cited books were not fully read.

deferred.reason: The study measures people’s ascriptions, not metaphysical possession, subjective machine experience or autonomous ethical conduct.

limitations: Zero additions; five existing attribution concepts directly enriched and one receives non-counted theoretical context. Catalogue remains819 in eleven categories. Embedded supplements are fully read; metadata, conditional arithmetic and unavailable original-data checks stay distinct.
